adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by can return nil (e.g. user emailed for a mention in a topic they never visited), so tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError and the unsubscribe link 500s

config/routes.rb:440 — State-changing unsubscribe is a plain GET without CSRF protection, so link prefetchers, mail scanners, or a cross-site tag can silently change a logged-in user's topic notification level

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds GET routes for `topics#unsubscribe` (config/routes.rb: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`). The controller action `TopicsController#unsubscribe` changes server state by toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!`. Because it is a plain GET (and `check_xhr` is explicitly skipped for `:unsubscribe`), this state change can be triggered by link prefetchers/mail scanners or cross-site requests (e.g., ``), and Rails CSRF protections generally do not apply to GET requests. This is a real security/correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — Unsubscribe toggles per visit (watching->regular on the first hit, then regular->muted), so the result depends on how many times the GET is hit and reloads or scanners escalate to muted

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the new logic explicitly toggles `TopicUser#notification_level` based on its current value: if `tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` it sets it to `:regular`, otherwise it sets it to `:muted` (see the `if/else` in the added `unsubscribe` action). This means repeated GETs to the unsubscribe URL will flip the state (e.g., watching/tracking -> regular on first hit, then regular -> muted on the next), so the final state depends on how many times the link is fetched (reloads, prefetchers, scanners, etc.), which is unintended for an "unsubscribe" endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — tu.save! skips TopicUser.change, so no MessageBus notification_level_change is published and notifications_reason_id is not updated, leaving open clients stale

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the code updates `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly. In this diff, `TopicUser.change` is the method that publishes `MessageBus` `/topic/#{topic_id}` with `{ notification_level_change: ... }` when `attrs[:notification_level]` is present. By bypassing `TopicUser.change`, no `notification_level_change` event is published, so any open clients relying on that bus channel can remain stale after an unsubscribe toggle.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6 — The page always says "You will stop receiving notifications" even when a watching/tracking user was only moved to regular and still gets reply/mention notifications

adjudication.rationale: The new unsubscribe UI always renders the string `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` via `stopNotificiationsText` (controller) and `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (template), but the server-side `TopicsController#unsubscribe` does not always fully unsubscribe/mute: if `tu.notification_level > :regular` it sets the level to `:regular` (otherwise to `:muted`). Therefore, for users coming from higher levels (e.g., tracking/watching), the page’s message “You will stop receiving notifications…” is not aligned with the actual state change performed by this diff (it only downgrades to regular).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:171 — Specs only pass unsubscribe_url to avoid the interpolation error and never assert the per-topic link appears; the controller unsubscribe action has no tests, so a broken feature would still pass

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the server locale `unsubscribe_link` to include `%{unsubscribe_url}` (config/locales/server.en.yml), and updates the spec to pass `unsubscribe_url` into `Email::MessageBuilder` (spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb) so interpolation won’t fail. However, nothing in the shown spec asserts that the rendered HTML actually contains the new per-topic unsubscribe link (it appears to only test the List-Unsubscribe header), so a regression where `%{unsubscribe_link}` is not substituted or the link text is wrong could still pass. Separately, a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action and routes are added with nontrivial behavior (toggling `TopicUser.notification_level`) and no tests are shown for it, leaving the feature unverified by automated tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:1855 — unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, so any future or plugin MessageBuilder caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without it will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb#html_part`, when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true it unconditionally calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`; `template_args` only includes `unsubscribe_url` if the caller passed it via opts (no default is set). The spec and `UserNotifications` caller were updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, but the API is now fragile/backwards-incompatible for any other caller (e.g., plugins or future code) that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without `unsubscribe_url`, which would raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — New GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe endpoint mutates notification state and toggles (tracking->regular, regular->muted) on every hit, so link prefetchers/repeat clicks silently mute the topic; state change should be idempotent or POST/confirm-driven.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicsController#unsubscribe` and routes it via `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` / `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`. Inside `unsubscribe`, it mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and *toggles* it (`> regular` -> `regular`, else -> `muted`) on every request, then `tu.save!`. Because this is a GET endpoint with side effects and non-idempotent behavior, repeated hits (including link prefetchers or accidental double-clicks) can silently change/mute notification state, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by may return nil (user notified via mention/category watch without a topic_users row), causing NoMethodError 500 on the emailed unsubscribe link.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and assigns to it. If `find_by` returns `nil` (no `topic_users` row exists for that user/topic), this will raise `NoMethodError` and 500 the request. The diff shows no guard/creation path (e.g., `TopicUser.change`/`find_or_create`) before dereferencing `tu`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:107 — List-Unsubscribe header still points to user preferences while the body now advertises a per-topic unsubscribe_url, so the machine-readable header and new contract diverge.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new `unsubscribe_url` option and expands the translated `unsubscribe_link` body text to include a per-topic link, but the diff does not show any code that sets or changes the `List-Unsubscribe` header (the header-building logic is not present in the shown `lib/email/message_builder.rb` hunk). Therefore, from the diff alone we cannot verify the claim that the header “still points to user preferences” or that it diverges from the new per-topic contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:1852 — unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but MessageBuilder does not default it, so any add_unsubscribe_link caller that omits unsubscribe_url (plugins/future mailers) renders a missing-interpolation string.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, `@template_args` provides defaults for `site_name`, `base_url`, and `user_preferences_url` but not `unsubscribe_url`, and `html_part` always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true. While the PR updates at least one caller (`UserNotifications#send_notification_email`) and a spec to pass `unsubscribe_url`, the diff does not prove all other existing callers do, nor does MessageBuilder guard/default it, creating a backward-compatibility/robustness risk (likely raising a MissingInterpolationArgument rather than rendering a string).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:109 — Non-idempotent GET toggles state: a second visit (reload, double click, or link prefetch/scanner) drops a regular user to muted, and watching users go only to regular on first visit, so the level depends on visit count.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a GET route/controller action `topics#unsubscribe` (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`) that mutates state by toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` between `:regular` and `:muted` based on current value (`if tu.notification_level > ... then regular else muted; tu.save!`). This is non-idempotent and a second visit/reload will flip the setting again, matching the finding’s described behavior (watching/tracking -> regular on first hit, then muted on second).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so no MessageBus notification_level_change is published and notifications_reason_id is left stale.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, it loads a `TopicUser` record and directly mutates `tu.notification_level` followed by `tu.save!`. Elsewhere in the codebase (shown in this diff), `TopicUser.change(...)` is the mechanism that publishes `MessageBus` `notification_level_change` events when `attrs[:notification_level]` is set. By bypassing `TopicUser.change`, this action will not publish that event, which can lead to stale notification state in clients relying on the MessageBus update. The finding’s additional claim about `notifications_reason_id` being left stale is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by can return nil (e.g. user notified via mention without a topic_users row) and tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError, causing a 500 on the unsubscribe link.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` is used immediately as `tu.notification_level` without checking for `nil`. If no `topic_users` row exists for that user/topic, this will raise `NoMethodError` and 500 the unsubscribe request. The diff does not establish that such a row is guaranteed to exist before hitting this action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — Non-idempotent state change on GET: each reload/prefetch/mail link-scanner hit steps level down again (watching->regular->muted), so a scanner or second click silently mutes the topic.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (added in this diff), a GET request to `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` mutates persistent state by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!`. The logic is non-idempotent for users coming from `tracking`/`watching` (levels `> regular`): first GET sets to `regular`, a subsequent GET (reload/link scanner/prefetch) then hits the `else` branch (`<= regular`) and sets to `muted`, silently stepping the user down further. This matches the finding and is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so no MessageBus notification_level_change is published and other open clients show stale notification state.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the code loads a `TopicUser` row and mutates `tu.notification_level` followed by `tu.save!` (direct ActiveRecord save). In this codebase, `TopicUser.change` is the method that also publishes `MessageBus` updates when `notification_level` changes (see `TopicUser.change` publishing `{ notification_level_change: ... }`). Since the unsubscribe path doesn’t call `TopicUser.change`, no `notification_level_change` message will be published for other open clients, so their UI can remain stale until a refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — State-changing unsubscribe action is exposed via GET with no CSRF token, so any third-party page/img tag can silently change a logged-in user's topic notification level (and repeated hits toggle regular -> muted).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that mutates state (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`) and is reachable via GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`). Since it’s a state-changing GET endpoint, it can be triggered cross-site (e.g., via an `` or link) without a CSRF token, and the implementation explicitly toggles the notification level between `regular` and `muted` on repeated hits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser lookup is not nil-checked, so any logged-in user hitting unsubscribe for a topic they have no TopicUser row for triggers a NoMethodError 500 instead of a handled response.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and later `tu.save!` without checking whether `tu` is nil. If no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic, this will raise a `NoMethodError` (500) on `tu.notification_level`, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — New unsubscribe action has no controller spec, so nil TopicUser (NoMethodError on tu.notification_level) and logged-out access paths are untested.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff shows `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` followed immediately by `tu.notification_level ...` and `tu.save!` with no nil-guard. If no `TopicUser` row exists, this will raise `NoMethodError`. Additionally, the action dereferences `current_user.id` without any shown login requirement/guard; a logged-out request would also error. These are real failure paths introduced by the new action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — Notification-level transitions (watching/tracking->regular, regular->muted, muted stays muted) have no test coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new notification-level transition logic in `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` between `:regular` and `:muted` depending on whether it was `> :regular`). The only test change shown is in `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` for `unsubscribe_url` in emails; no controller/request/model spec is added covering the new transition behavior in `topics_controller.rb`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172 — Spec only adds unsubscribe_url to avoid an interpolation error and never asserts the per-topic unsubscribe link appears in the body.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new interpolation key `%{unsubscribe_url}` to the `unsubscribe_link` server locale string, and MessageBuilder renders it into the HTML via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` (lib/email/message_builder.rb). The spec change only updates `message_with_unsubscribe` to pass `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"`, and the shown example still only asserts the `List-Unsubscribe` header, not that the per-topic unsubscribe link text/URL is present in the rendered body. This is a specific test-coverage gap for newly introduced behavior, not a runtime bug proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:90 — No test covers add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url, which now raises I18n MissingInterpolationArgument for any caller omitting it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` with no default for `unsubscribe_url`, so calling `Email::MessageBuilder` with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but without `unsubscribe_url` would raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`. The updated spec only covers the case where `unsubscribe_url` is provided, so this edge-case is untested and could break any existing callers not updated (only `user_notifications.rb` is shown updated in this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic.rb:719 — Topic#unsubscribe_url and the mailer passing it (user_notifications.rb:295) have no model or mailer spec.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new Topic#unsubscribe_url method (app/models/topic.rb) and starts passing unsubscribe_url into the notification email opts (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb). The only related spec change is in message_builder_spec.rb, which supplies an unsubscribe_url directly; there is no new/updated spec in the diff exercising Topic#unsubscribe_url itself or verifying that the mailer provides the correct unsubscribe_url for a real post/topic. This is a test coverage gap for newly introduced behavior, not a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:1 — New Ember route/controller/template and dropdown-button title change ship with no JS tests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new client-side behavior (new Ember route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, controller/template/view, and a behavioral change in `dropdown-button` to only render the title when present) but the PR diff does not add or modify any JavaScript/QUnit/Ember tests covering this new route flow or the dropdown rendering change (the only test change shown is a Ruby spec in `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than an immediately verifiable runtime defect.
